JOB OVERVIEW

General Mills is seeking an E-Commerce Packaging Engineer in their Pet Segment Operating Unit. This role will have Packaging R&D accountability for iconic brands, including BLUE Buffalo and EdgardCooper. You will serve as the direct Packaging R&D business interface across these key brands to deliver the current plan and partner on growth strategies, and build packaging capability to enable the future growth for Pet. This role will coordinate across a talented team of technical leaders, execute against innovation growth ideas, core renovation levers, and advance our digital transformation capabilities for our e-commerce channel.

This role will create and translate a Packaging modeling framework to help accelerate our flexible format across all of Pet with an emphasis on e-commerce. This responsibility spans across a large raw material cost of goods sold and requires strong activation and leadership to deliver against innovation and cost savings goals.

You will manage a portfolio of products through a complex manufacturing network, temperature states, and channels, providing opportunities to lead new ways of working with a variety of cross-functional partners.

• Develop a flexible technology framework through new digital ways of working across the entire Pet portfolio.

• Support and activate a packaging strategy to unlock fewer and bigger end-to-end cost savings initiatives.

• Drive key business initiatives to drive growth for our business in a variety of formats and business sectors, including e-commerce partnerships and non-traditional bag formats

• Steer the activation of functional and business strategies by driving moments of truth levers, tapping into subject matter experts, external partners, and brand remarkability tools to drive a packaging growth agenda.

• Advance a Circular Future through business management and collaboration with central technology resources on new packaging material technologies to drive the advancement of Global Responsibility commitments for packaging sustainability.

• Bachelor's Degree in Packaging Engineering or other related degree fields

• 5 years of packaging experience working in CPG packaging or other relevant industry, with 3+ years working on e-commerce packaging.

• Experience and technical acumen across a variety of packaging materials, including flexible films and thermal rigid plastics.

• Demonstrated knowledge of business processes and ability to develop relationships with cross-functional partners.

• Demonstrated strong people skills, strategic planning, and leadership skills

• Desire to challenge assumptions, identify new opportunities, and create new ways of working & capabilities.

• Effective communication skills to influence internal and external stakeholders

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Takes accountability to win, has a bias for action, and can deliver results through others.

• Depth and experience in designing, qualifying, and commercializing dry pet food packaging across an array of size offerings for all channels.

• Mentoring and coaching others for growth.

• Experience in mentoring and developing other packaging engineers or team members.

• Comfortable navigating ambiguity and organizational complexity.

• Demonstrated strong agile leadership & ability to pivot quickly.

• Exceptional multi-tasking, follow-up, and prioritization skills.

Your role at Clorox

At Clorox, Packaging is a critical part of the consumer experience, brand equity, sustainability journey, and business growth strategy. As a Scientist II within Packaging R&D for the Cleaning Business Unit, you will develop and deliver packaging solutions that delight consumers, enable manufacturing excellence, and drive profitable growth across some of the most trusted household brands.

This role is ideal for an engineer or scientist who enjoys solving complex technical challenges, influencing cross-functional teams, and turning consumer insights into innovative packaging solutions. You'll lead packaging development initiatives from concept through commercialization, working at the intersection of consumer needs, sustainability, manufacturing, supply chain, and business strategy.

As a Scientist II, you will operate with increasing independence, often navigating ambiguity and driving solutions where design, manufacturing approaches, technical requirements, or business needs are still being defined.

Join Clorox and help shape the future of packaging for brands used in millions of homes every day. You'll have the opportunity to solve meaningful technical challenges, influence the direction of iconic brands, and create packaging innovations that deliver superior consumer experiences while advancing sustainability and business growth. If you're energized by turning ideas into products that reach store shelves and consumers' homes, we'd love to meet you.

In this role, you will:

Lead Packaging Development

• Own packaging development projects from concept through commercialization, including design, testing, qualification, scale-up, and launch.
• Develop primary, secondary, club, and e-commerce packaging solutions that balance consumer experience, performance, sustainability, cost, and manufacturability.
• Drive packaging solutions for new products, line extensions, and cost savings.
Solve Technical Challenges

• Lead packaging development efforts where package design, manufacturing approaches, or technical requirements may be undefined or evolving.
• Apply engineering and scientific principles to troubleshoot packaging, manufacturing, and supply chain challenges.
• Assess technical risks and develop mitigation plans to deliver successful business outcomes.
Influence Across the Organization

• Partner closely with Marketing, Product Development, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Procurement, Quality, Regulatory, Sales, and external suppliers.
• Effectively communicate technical recommendations and influence decisions with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
• Support claims, demonstrations, and business cases to help drive project alignment and decision-making.
Commercialize with Excellence

Packaging Lead Engineer

In this role you will be responsible for setting up the enterprise packaging strategy and technology roadmap while leading a group of engineers.

Develop, implement, and maintain comprehensive process standards and documentation to support all end-to-end packaging business and engineering workflows.

Establish packaging standards and lead execution of automation, returnable, and expendable plans while setting the standard on how Autoliv will achieve cost, quality, and sustainability goals. Assign workload to a team of engineers for new launch.

Should you be interested in overseeing these tasks and aiming for enhanced performance standards, your role will involve :

What you'll do

• Establish and maintain packaging standards for automation, returnable, and expendable execution; publish controlled specifications and playbooks

• Lead governance for exceptions/waivers; chair the standards review board and manage change control (ECO/ECN)

• Define common footprints and automation execution standards; align with safety/quality and sustainability requirements.

• Own enterprise packaging data architecture and tools (spec/PFEP, cartonization, labeling, image vaults): governance, permissions, and data-quality SLAs.

• Standardize master data (part-to-pack links, dunnage IDs, test results, sustainability attributes) and audit routines; lead training and adoption.

• Select/administer cartonization and labeling systems (GS1/AIAG compliant), including template libraries and formal change control.

• Set/enforce ID standards (serialization, barcode/QR/RFID), labeling, and traceability checkpoints (ship/receive scans, gate checks).

• Own the portfolio/roadmap for packaging materials, formats, and automation; prioritize pilots with success criteria and scale proven solutions.

• Conduct market/technology scouting; partner with suppliers/startups to mature innovations into standards.

• Develop KPIs/dashboards; monitor compliance and drive corrective actions with site leaders.

• Mentor regional teams; build capability via training, playbooks, and office hours

• Lead and set workload for a team of packaging engineers for new model launch and serialization projects

What is required

• BS in Packaging Engineering (preferred) or ME/IE

• 7–10+ years in packaging or logistics engineering, including multi-site standards/systems ownership in automotive/Tier-1 or similar high-volume manufacturing.

• Hands-on with PFEP/spec databases, cartonization (TOPS/Cape or WMS-native), labeling, and GS1/AIAG compliance.

• Experience integrating packaging data with ERP/PLM/WMS (e.g., SAP/Oracle; Teamcenter/Windchill); strong Excel/BI; familiarity with APIs/MDM concepts.

• Working knowledge of ISTA/ASTM transit testing, load-securement, and sustainability/EPR considerations.

• CAD & Packaging: SolidWorks/NX/CATIA; ArtiosCAD for corrugated/dunnage; read drawings, GD&T, basic tolerance stacks.

• Attractive compensation package

• Recognition awards, company events, family events, university discount options and many more perks.

• Gender Pay Equality
